annotation.title_clean: Welfare Technology Developers’ Views Concerning Responsible Innovation and Implementation of Care Robots in Ireland and Japan
annotation.title_en: Welfare Technology Developers’ Views Concerning Responsible Innovation and Implementation of Care Robots in Ireland and Japan
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Kodate, N.; Maeda, Y.; Yumoto, A.; Donnelly, S.; Tsujimura, M.; Mannan, H.; et al.
annotation.venue: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence and Applications, Vol. 397 (Robophilosophy 2024), IOS Press
annotation.summary_en: Conference paper reporting semi-structured interviews with 14 welfare technology developers in Ireland and Japan on responsible robotics in care. Developers believe care robots can strengthen long-term care if ethical aspects are considered, and recommend curricula/training inclusion and correcting skewed media portrayals.
key_provisions_or_claims: Developers believe care robots would strengthen long-term care systems if ethics are considered
Uniform long-term care system eases top-down introduction but can widen mismatch with user needs
Recommends including welfare technology in professional curricula and training
Recommends changing skewed media representation of AI and robotics
